tone.target: clean disco-pop guitar with light chorus
tone.profile: clean disco-pop guitar with light chorus
tone.summary: A pristine signal chain utilizing a Boost for initial brightness, followed by Chorus and Comp for rhythmic definition, leading into the US Deluxe amp model with a clear 2x12 cabinet to capture the required Fender-esque clarity.

rig.name: The Doobie Brothers - What A Fool Believes - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and maintain tight rhythm playing.
Enhance the initial attack and brightness required for disco-pop rhythm.
blocks.gap: The Boost module is used to simulate a clean, bright boost pedal (like an early overdrive or volume booster) without adding grit.

blocks.purpose: Provide tight, consistent rhythm and punch for muted disco chords.
Add the required subtle, shimmering chorus effect characteristic of 80s pop/disco.
Keep the tone clean and transparent; no distortion needed.
blocks.gap: The 'None' model is used to ensure zero signal degradation or unwanted grit.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the clean, bright, single-coil driven sound of a Fender/JC-120 style amp.
blocks.gap: The US Deluxe is the closest available model to achieve the required vintage American clean tone.

blocks.purpose: Provide a bright, articulate, and focused cabinet sound suitable for clean pop tones.
Fine-tune the frequency response to emphasize clarity and 'air' in the high end.
Add subtle depth and space without muddying the tight rhythm.
blocks.gap: Plate reverb is ideal for pop/disco as it adds shimmer without excessive wash.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism to better capture the vintage American pop sound.

proposals.reason: Enhance clarity and vintage character for disco-pop rhythm.
